title: Wyoming Driver License Practice Test — Class C
subtitle: Rules of the Road, 2021
source: Wyoming Rules of the Road Driver License Manual, 2021 (Wyoming Department of Transportation, Driver Services Program)
notes: Questions and answer wording are drawn closely from the source manual. `correct` is a zero-based index into the `answers` array.

questions.question: A 16½-year-old applicant may obtain full driving privileges by meeting which requirement?
answers: Holding an instruction permit for one year after passing the vision screening
Holding a restricted license for one year after passing the vision screening
Completing driver education and holding an intermediate license for six months
Completing driver education and holding a restricted license for six months
questions.explanation: For full driving privileges, an applicant must be at least 17, or be 16½ and have completed an approved driver education course and held an intermediate license for six months.

questions.question: At what age may an instruction permit be obtained in Wyoming?
questions.explanation: An instruction permit may be obtained at 15. At 16, an applicant may obtain limited driving privileges by acquiring an intermediate license.

questions.question: The Class C license authorizes operation of a single vehicle or combination of vehicles, except motorcycles, with a GVWR of:
answers: less than 26,001 pounds
less than 10,000 pounds
less than 16,000 pounds
26,001 pounds or more
questions.explanation: The Class C license authorizes operation of a single vehicle or combination of vehicles, except motorcycles, with a GVWR less than 26,001 pounds, or any such vehicle towing another which does not have a GVWR in excess of 10,000 pounds.

questions.question: Under the Class C license, you may tow another vehicle that does not have a GVWR in excess of:
answers: 26,001 pounds
16,000 pounds
5,000 pounds
10,000 pounds
questions.explanation: A Class C license allows operation of a vehicle with a GVWR less than 26,001 pounds, or any such vehicle towing another which does not have a GVWR in excess of 10,000 pounds.

questions.question: Licensees over 21 may renew their Wyoming driver license within what period preceding expiration?
answers: 30 days
120 days
60 days
90 days
questions.explanation: Licensees over 21 may renew within the 120-day period preceding expiration. Licensees under 21 may renew within 90 days of expiration.

questions.question: What is the fee for an original Wyoming non-commercial driver license, before the additional technology fee?
questions.explanation: Non-commercial fees: Original Wyoming License $40, Restricted License $20, Renewal $30, Renewal by Mail $30, Instruction Permit $40, Intermediate License $30. An additional technology fee of $5 applies to all classes.

questions.question: A person licensed by another state which is a Driver License Compact member may drive in Wyoming on that out-of-state license, but must surrender it within what period of residency in Wyoming?
answers: 90 days
Six months
One year
Two years
questions.explanation: Any person licensed by another Compact member state does not need a Wyoming license unless they choose one; however, their out-of-state license must be surrendered within one year of residency in Wyoming.

questions.question: When Wyoming licensees change their addresses, they must notify the department in writing within:
answers: 20 days
90 days
30 days
10 days
questions.explanation: When licensees change their addresses, they must notify the department in writing within 10 days of the change.

questions.question: To meet Wyoming vision standards for operating a motor vehicle, a person must have:
answers: 20/40 acuity in one eye, with or without glasses
20/40 acuity with both eyes, and a combined horizontal field of vision of at least 120 degrees
20/30 acuity with both eyes, and a combined horizontal field of vision of at least 100 degrees
20/60 acuity with both eyes, and a combined horizontal field of vision of at least 180 degrees
questions.explanation: A person must have 20/40 acuity with both eyes, either with or without glasses, and a combined horizontal field vision of at least 120 degrees to meet Wyoming vision standards.

questions.question: Applicants for a Wyoming driver license are allowed to take the written test how many times in one day?
answers: Twice
Unlimited
Once
Three times
questions.explanation: Applicants for a driver's license are allowed to take the written test twice in one day.

questions.question: An applicant who fails the Wyoming skills test must wait how long before testing again?
answers: 24 hours
Three days
One week
48 hours
questions.explanation: Applicants who fail the skills test must wait 24 hours before testing again. A three-day wait applies when an applicant misses 13 or more questions.

questions.question: The skills test may be waived by presenting a certification card. What must that card state the student has completed?
answers: 10 hours of classroom instruction and 2 hours of behind-the-wheel driving
36 hours of classroom instruction and 8 hours of behind-the-wheel driving
30 hours of classroom instruction and 6 hours of behind-the-wheel driving
20 hours of classroom instruction and 4 hours of behind-the-wheel driving
questions.explanation: The certification card must state that the student has completed 30 hours of classroom instruction and six hours of behind-the-wheel driving. The card will be honored for no longer than two years.

questions.question: If your visual acuity is worse than 20/40 but at least 20/100, you will be required to:
answers: Obtain a vision statement from an eye specialist and may not drive
Wear corrective lenses and retake the vision screening only
Take a driving skills test
Apply for a restricted license
questions.explanation: Those who fail the vision screening must obtain a vision statement from an eye specialist. If visual acuity is worse than 20/40 but at least 20/100, you will be required to take a driving skills test.

questions.question: An Administrative Per Se Suspension results when you are arrested for DWUI and the results of your chemical test show an alcohol concentration of:
answers: 0.02 percent or greater
0.15 percent or greater
0.08 percent or greater
0.04 percent or greater
questions.explanation: An Administrative Per Se Suspension results when you have been arrested for DWUI and the results of your chemical test show an alcohol concentration of 0.08 percent or greater.

questions.question: What is the length of the Administrative Per Se suspension?
answers: 90 days
One year
30 days
60 days
questions.explanation: Length of suspension: 90 days. If you are convicted of the DWUI in court, the time served for the Administrative Per Se suspension will be credited toward the DWUI suspension.

questions.question: What effect does dismissal of a DWUI in court have on the Administrative Per Se suspension?
answers: Dismissal in court does not affect it
Dismissal reduces it by half
Dismissal removes it from your record
Dismissal suspends it until the case closes
questions.explanation: The Administrative Per Se suspension is imposed by the Department based on the chemical test result at the time of arrest, so it stands on its own. If you are instead convicted of the DWUI in court, the time you served on the Per Se suspension is credited toward the DWUI suspension.

questions.question: For a first DWUI offense within the previous 10 years, the length of suspension is:
answers: Six months
90 days
One year
Three years
questions.explanation: 1st offense (within previous 10 years) — Length of suspension: 90 days. If you served or are serving a suspension for Administrative Per Se, the suspension period will be the same.

questions.question: A second DWUI offense within the previous 10 years results in a suspension of:
answers: Six months
One year
Two years
90 days
questions.explanation: 2nd offense (within previous 10 years) — Length of suspension: One year. If you served or are serving a suspension for Administrative Per Se, an additional nine-month suspension will be added to your record.

questions.question: A third or subsequent DWUI within 10 years results in a:
answers: Lifetime revocation
Three-year revocation
One-year suspension
Two-year suspension
questions.explanation: 3rd or subsequent offense (within 10 years) — Length of revocation: Three years.

questions.question: If you are younger than 21 and are in actual physical control of a vehicle with an alcohol concentration of 0.02 percent or more, you will be suspended for DWUI. For a first offense, the length of suspension is:
answers: 90 days
Six months
30 days
60 days
questions.explanation: Youthful Driver Suspension — First offense: Length of suspension 90 days. Second or subsequent offense (within two years): Six months.

questions.question: According to the manual, which of the following is one of the three factors that influence Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC)?
answers: The person's age
The person's body weight
The person's gender
The person's height
questions.explanation: The manual lists the amount of alcohol consumed, the period over which it is consumed, and the person's body weight. Age, gender, and height are not among its three factors.

questions.question: Approximately what percentage of the alcohol in your body is eliminated by the liver, and at what rate?
answers: About 90 percent, at a constant rate of about one drink per hour
About 50 percent, at a rate of one drink every 30 minutes
About 100 percent, at a constant rate of one drink per hour
About 90 percent, at a rate of one drink every two hours
questions.explanation: Approximately 90 percent of the alcohol in your body is eliminated by the liver. It is eliminated at a constant rate, about the same for all persons, about one drink per hour. It CANNOT be eliminated any faster.

questions.question: Which of the following will reduce the level of alcohol in your body?
answers: Only time
Taking a shower
Drinking coffee
Exercising vigorously
questions.explanation: Showering, drinking coffee or exercising in an effort to sober up are useless. Only time can do the job. Time is the only significant factor in reducing BAC levels.

questions.question: Which of the following contains about one-half ounce of alcohol?
answers: 12 ounces of beer
12 ounces of wine
3 ounces of 86 proof hard liquor
6 ounces of beer
questions.explanation: 12 ounces of beer, 3 to 5 ounces of wine, and 1.5 ounces of 86 proof hard liquor each contain about one-half ounce of alcohol. 12 ounces of wine and 3 ounces of liquor contain more; 6 ounces of beer contains less.

questions.question: According to the manual, a BAC of 0.08 percent is considered to be:
answers: Low for most drivers, but high for inexperienced drivers
High, with impairment whether or not outward signs show
Low, since outward signs determine impairment
High only for drivers under 21
questions.explanation: A BAC of 0.02 percent is considered low. A BAC of 0.08 percent is considered high, and people at that level are impaired mentally and physically whether or not they show it.

questions.question: A drinking driver traveling at 55 mph will drive an additional distance of at least how far before he can apply the brakes?
answers: 32 feet
22 feet
12 feet
55 feet
questions.explanation: Because of this reduced ability to execute, a drinking driver, traveling at 55 mph, will drive an additional 32 feet or more before he can apply the brakes.

questions.question: If convicted of a first DWUI with a BAC of .15 percent or greater, how long must you hold an ignition interlock restricted driver license before you are eligible for any other type of driver license?
answers: Two years
Six months
Three months
One year
questions.explanation: If your BAC at the time of arrest was .15% or greater, you will be required to hold an ignition interlock restricted driver license for a period of 6 months before you are eligible for any other type of driver license.

questions.question: If convicted of a 4th or subsequent DWUI when alcohol is involved, the ignition interlock requirement is:
answers: Ten years, with removal available after five
Five years, with removal available after two
Lifetime, with removal available after five years
Two years, with removal available after one year
questions.explanation: A 4th or subsequent alcohol-related DWUI requires a lifetime ignition interlock; you may petition for removal five years after the conviction date.

questions.question: Driving while under the influence of alcohol is the major cause of what?
answers: One quarter of all injury crashes
Most crashes involving motorcycles
Almost half of all fatal crashes
Every crash involving a teenage driver
questions.explanation: Alcohol is involved in almost half of all fatal crashes. Nationwide, nearly 25,000 people die each year because of drinking drivers.

questions.question: The impairment of alcohol is described in the manual as seriously reducing the ability to IDENTIFY, PREDICT, DECIDE and what else?
answers: COMMUNICATE
EXECUTE
REACT
ADJUST
questions.explanation: Alcohol seriously impairs the ability to drive safely because the ability to IDENTIFY, PREDICT, DECIDE and EXECUTE is seriously reduced.

questions.question: According to the legal speed limits in the manual (all unless otherwise posted), what is the speed limit in a school zone?
answers: 25 mph
15 mph
20 mph
30 mph
questions.explanation: School Zones: 20 mph. The absolute speed limit in a school zone is 20 mph.

questions.question: What is the legal speed limit on secondary highways in Wyoming, unless otherwise posted?
answers: 65 mph
70 mph
75 mph
55 mph
questions.explanation: Legal speed limits (All unless otherwise posted): Interstate Highways 80 mph, 75 mph; Secondary Highways 70 mph; Residential Areas 30 mph; Business Areas 30 mph; School Zones 20 mph.

questions.question: The legal speed limit in both residential areas and business areas is:
answers: 25 mph
20 mph
30 mph
15 mph
questions.explanation: Residential Areas: 30 mph. Business Areas: 30 mph.

questions.question: What are the legal speed limits on Interstate Highways in Wyoming, unless otherwise posted?
answers: 75 mph, 80 mph
80 mph, 85 mph
70 mph, 75 mph
65 mph, 70 mph
questions.explanation: Wyoming posts two speed limits on Interstate highways: 80 mph and 75 mph. The manual also lists 70 mph for secondary highways, 30 mph in residential and business areas, and 20 mph in school zones.

questions.question: Trees, bushes or buildings at intersections can block the view of vehicles coming from the side. You should approach a blind intersection at no more than:
answers: 15 mph
10 mph
5 mph
25 mph
questions.explanation: Trees, bushes or buildings at intersections can block the view of vehicles coming from the side. Therefore approach a blind intersection at no more than 15 mph.

questions.question: When driving on a curve, you should:
answers: Adjust speed after you are well into the curve
Maintain your speed through the curve
Adjust speed BEFORE entering the curve
Sound your horn before entering the curve
questions.explanation: Adjust speed BEFORE entering a curve. Going too fast can break the grip that tires have on the road.

questions.question: According to the manual's table for slippery roads, when driving on packed snow you should reduce your speed by at least:
answers: Half
5 to 10 mph
A crawl
One quarter
questions.explanation: Slippery roads reduce the tires' grip, so drive slower than you would on a dry road. Wet road: reduce speed by at least 5-10 mph. Packed snow: reduce speed by at least half. Ice: reduce speed to a crawl.

questions.question: According to the manual, when driving on ice you should:
answers: Maintain your normal speed
Reduce speed by at least 5-10 mph
Reduce speed to a crawl
Reduce speed by at least half
questions.explanation: Ice — Reduce speed to a crawl. You may have to slow even more if vehicles are ahead.

questions.question: Your headlights let you see clearly about 250 feet ahead. Driving faster than 55 mph on a dark road means you are:
answers: Driving within the legal speed limit
Driving blind beyond your stopping distance
Seeing well enough to react in time
Driving with adequate visibility
questions.explanation: Never drive so fast that you cannot stop within the distance you can see ahead. At night your headlights clearly show about 250 feet, so above 55 mph you are driving blind.

questions.question: According to the manual, going slower than traffic or stopping suddenly is:
answers: Safe, because you are not speeding
As dangerous as speeding
Dangerous only when passing another vehicle
Only dangerous at night
questions.explanation: Going slower than traffic or stopping suddenly is as dangerous as speeding. The risk of rear-end collisions is added to the risk of vehicles passing you.

questions.question: At an intersection with no signs or signals, you must yield the right of way to:
answers: Any driver coming from your right
The vehicle going straight ahead
The vehicle that reached the intersection first
The vehicle on your left
questions.explanation: Where no signs or signals are in place, you must watch for any driver coming from your right and yield the right of way regardless of who first reaches and enters the intersection.

questions.question: According to the manual, right-of-way laws:
answers: Give you the right to go first if you arrive first
Only indicate who must yield the right of way
Apply only to four-way stop intersections
Apply only when signs are posted
questions.explanation: Laws do not give anyone the right of way. They only indicate who must yield the right of way.

questions.question: At a four-way stop intersection, the driver who stops first should be permitted to go first. If in doubt, you should:
answers: Proceed first if you are going straight
Sound your horn and proceed
Insist on your right of way
Yield to the driver on your right
questions.explanation: IF IN DOUBT, YIELD TO THE DRIVER ON YOUR RIGHT. Never insist on the right of way at the risk of a crash.

questions.question: Traffic in a roundabout moves:
answers: Counterclockwise, at highway speeds
Counterclockwise, at slow speeds
Clockwise, at slow speeds
Clockwise, unless otherwise posted
questions.explanation: Traffic moves at slow speeds in a counterclockwise direction, and is constantly moving except when yielding to traffic in the roundabout and pedestrians in the crosswalks.

questions.question: When entering a roundabout, you should:
answers: Look left, wait for a gap, and merge
Look right, wait for a gap, and merge
Stop in the center until traffic clears
Enter without yielding if the way looks clear
questions.explanation: Look to the left, wait for a gap in traffic and merge into the roundabout. Once in the roundabout, keep moving, don't stop.

questions.question: When leaving a roundabout, you should:
answers: Signal and yield to pedestrians as you exit
Yield to circulating traffic before signaling
Exit and merge without signaling
Stop and signal after leaving the roundabout
questions.explanation: Once in the roundabout, keep moving and do not stop. Proceed to your exit, use your turn signal to indicate you are leaving, and yield to pedestrians as you leave.

questions.question: If you enter an intersection while violating the speed law, you:
answers: Retain any right of way you might have had
Have equal right of way with everyone else
Must yield only to vehicles on your right
Forfeit any right of way you might have had
questions.explanation: At a four-way stop, common courtesy gives the right to go first to the driver who stops first, and if you are in doubt you should yield to the driver on your right. Entering an intersection while violating the speed law gives up that advantage: you forfeit any right of way you might have had and must be prepared to yield.

questions.question: When you hear the siren or see the flashing lights of an emergency vehicle approaching you from behind, you should:
answers: Pull to the right curb and stop
Stop in the intersection to clear the way
Continue until the emergency vehicle passes
Speed up so it can pass on the left
questions.explanation: Pull as close as possible to the right-hand curb or edge of the roadway and stop. Do not stop in an intersection. Remain stopped until the emergency vehicle has passed.

questions.question: When pulling over for an emergency vehicle, the manual says to keep your foot on the brake so that:
answers: Your engine keeps running and the battery charges
The vehicle behind you knows to stop
The emergency driver knows you are stopped
Your brake lights stay on for visibility
questions.explanation: Keep your foot on the brake so the emergency driver knows you are stopped.

questions.question: On roads with only one lane in each direction, you must reduce your speed to at least how much below the speed limit when approaching a parked emergency vehicle?
answers: 15 mph
10 mph
5 mph
20 mph
questions.explanation: On roads with only one lane in each direction, you must reduce your speed to at least 20 mph below the speed limit when approaching a parked emergency vehicle. On a road with two or more lanes, the rule is to merge into the lane farthest from the emergency vehicle instead.

questions.question: When driving on a highway with two or more lanes traveling in the same direction, upon approaching an authorized emergency vehicle or other vehicle parked with lights flashing or visual signals, you must:
answers: Stop behind the parked vehicle
Continue at your current speed and lane
Pull onto the shoulder and stop
Merge into the lane farthest from it
questions.explanation: When driving on a highway with two or more lanes, you must merge your vehicle into the lane farthest from the emergency vehicle.

questions.question: Under Wyoming law, when must you yield to a pedestrian?
answers: Only when the pedestrian is on the sidewalk
For a pedestrian in a marked crosswalk on your side
Only when a school zone is posted
Only at night or in bad weather
questions.explanation: You must yield to a pedestrian in a marked crosswalk on your side of the roadway, whether or not there are signals. You must also yield when making a lawful turn on red after a complete stop and to a blind pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog.

questions.question: On a two or four lane undivided highway, when a school bus stops with flashing red lights, you must:
answers: Pass only if you are more than 10 mph faster than the bus
Stop, regardless of which direction you are traveling
Stop only if you are traveling in the same direction as the bus
Slow down and proceed with extreme caution
questions.explanation: On a two or four lane undivided highway, vehicles going each direction must stop when a school bus stops.

questions.question: You may pass a school bus with activated flashing red lights only if:
answers: A physical barrier or separate roadway separates you
The bus has been stopped for less than 10 seconds
The bus is stopped on the shoulder
The road has four or more lanes
questions.explanation: You may pass a school bus with activated flashing red lights only if there is a physical barrier or separate roadways between your vehicle and the school bus. You MUST use extreme caution, however, watching for pedestrians.

questions.question: On a divided roadway, when a school bus stops with flashing red lights, which vehicles must stop?
answers: No vehicles must stop
Only vehicles approaching from behind the bus
Only vehicles on the same side as the bus
All vehicles in both directions
questions.explanation: However, on a divided roadway, only vehicles on the same side of the separation as the bus must stop.

questions.question: You MUST stop your vehicle for:
answers: Pedestrians in a crosswalk only when the light is red
Pedestrians jogging on the shoulder
Any pedestrian standing at the edge of the road
A blind person crossing with a white cane or guide dog
questions.explanation: Blind pedestrians get a required stop of their own: you must stop for anyone attempting to cross a street who is carrying a white cane or is guided by a guide dog. You must also stop before the crosswalk at a stop sign, a red light or flashing red lights, and for a police officer, whose directions outweigh traffic lights or signs.

questions.question: Which of the following requires you to stop your vehicle?
answers: A pedestrian walking along the side of the road
A flag person at a construction site
A vehicle parked on the shoulder
A bicyclist riding in your lane
questions.explanation: The manual requires a stop when signaled by a flag person at or near railroad crossings or construction sites. A pedestrian walking along the roadside, a parked vehicle, or a bicyclist does not by itself require a stop.

questions.question: A police officer's directions:
answers: Are overridden by posted speed limits
Apply only if the officer is a highway patrol officer
Outweigh traffic lights or signs
Apply only at four-way stops
questions.explanation: When directed to do so by a police officer. A police officer's directions outweigh traffic lights or signs.

questions.question: All drivers must signal at least how far from an intersection?
answers: 200 feet
50 feet
150 feet
100 feet
questions.explanation: All drivers must signal when turning or changing lanes, and at least 100 feet from an intersection. Signaling at least 4 to 5 seconds BEFORE you wish to turn is better at higher speeds.

questions.question: The hand and arm signal for a right turn is:
answers: Extended down from the elbow
Extended straight out to the right
Extended straight up from the elbow
Extended straight out to the left
questions.explanation: For a right turn, the hand and arm are extended straight up from the elbow. For a left turn, the driver's hand and arm are extended straight out to the left. To slow down or stop, the hand and arm are extended down from the elbow.

questions.question: When may you change lanes in relation to an intersection?
answers: Before entering it
While in it, if you signal
Neither before nor while in it
Only if no one is on your right
questions.explanation: A lane change takes time and space that nobody inside an intersection expects you to use. Finish your lane changes first, and do not change lanes before or while in an intersection.

questions.question: Before changing lanes, you should:
answers: Check only your rearview and side mirrors
Signal, then change lanes without checking
Check mirrors, blind spots, and other drivers before signaling
Check over your shoulder, then change lanes immediately
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes: check in your rear view and side mirrors; check over your left or right shoulder and make sure no one is in your blind spots; check for other drivers who may also be moving into the same lane; and signal and change lanes.

questions.question: Before you back up your vehicle, the manual says to:
answers: Sound your horn and back up slowly
Rely on your rearview mirror
Rely on your side mirrors
Walk behind it and turn your head and body
questions.explanation: Check behind your vehicle by walking behind it before you back up. When you back up, do not depend upon your mirrors. Turn your head and body so that you can see where you are backing.

questions.question: While passing another vehicle that is traveling at less than the legal maximum speed, a driver may exceed the speed limit by up to:
answers: 5 mph
20 mph
10 mph
15 mph
questions.explanation: MOVE BACK into the right lane when you see the front of the vehicle in your rear view mirror. A driver may exceed the speed limit by up to 10 miles an hour while passing another vehicle that is traveling at less than the legal maximum speed.

questions.question: When passing, the manual says to START:
answers: At least one second behind the vehicle ahead
At least three seconds behind the vehicle ahead
Alongside the vehicle ahead
At least two seconds behind the vehicle ahead
questions.explanation: DECIDE if it is necessary to pass, then: START at least two seconds behind the vehicle ahead. MAKE SURE you have time and space to pass safely.

questions.question: When passing a bicyclist, you should reduce your speed and, when space allows, maintain at least how much separation between your vehicle and the bicyclist?
answers: 1 foot
6 feet
3 feet
2 feet
questions.explanation: When passing a bicyclist, reduce your speed to reduce the danger of a crash. When space allows, maintain at least 3 feet of separation between your vehicle and the bicyclist.

questions.question: Motorcycles are entitled to the same full lane width as all other vehicles. You should:
answers: Move into the same lane alongside a motorcycle, even if the lane is wide and the cyclist is far to one side
Follow motorcycles at one second
Never move into the same lane alongside a motorcycle
Pass motorcycles only in the right lane
questions.explanation: Never move into the same lane alongside a motorcycle, even if the lane is wide and the cyclist is riding far to one side. It is not only illegal, but it boxes both of you in and does not permit you a way out.

questions.question: On a two-lane road, you are required to:
answers: Drive in the center of the roadway
Keep to the shoulder where possible
Drive on the right and yield the left half to oncoming traffic
Drive on the left and yield the right half to oncoming traffic
questions.explanation: On a two-lane road (one lane going in each direction) you are required to drive on the right side and to yield the left half of the roadway to oncoming traffic.

questions.question: When there are three or more lanes going in one direction, which lane is usually the smoothest flow of traffic?
answers: The middle lane or lanes
The inside lane
The right lane
The left lane
questions.explanation: When there are three or more lanes going in one direction, the middle lane or lanes are usually the smoothest. The left lane is for drivers who want to go faster, pass or turn left. Slower drivers and those turning right use the right lane.

questions.question: Which sign shape is reserved for stop signs?
answers: Octagon (eight sides)
Diamond
Pennant
Pentagon
questions.explanation: Octagon (eight sides): This shape is reserved for stop signs. You must come to a complete stop.

questions.question: Which sign shape warns of a school zone ahead or marks a school crossing?
answers: Triangle pointing down
Pentagon
Rectangle
Round
questions.explanation: Pentagon: This sign warns of a school zone ahead or marks a school crossing. The absolute speed limit in a school zone is 20 mph.

questions.question: Pennant-shaped signs are located:
answers: At the beginning of a no-passing zone
At the end of a no-passing zone
At railroad crossings
At the end of a school zone
questions.explanation: A pennant marks the point where a no-passing zone begins; the zone itself is marked by solid yellow lines, and crossing them to pass or change lanes is not permitted unless you are making a left turn into or from an alley, private road or driveway. The end of the zone is not marked with a pennant.

questions.question: A round sign warns of:
answers: A no-passing zone ahead
A railroad crossing ahead
A change in speed limit
A school zone ahead
questions.explanation: A round sign warns of a railroad crossing ahead. Instead, a stop line or an X with the letters RR may be painted on the pavement before a crossing.

questions.question: Construction and maintenance warning signs are:
answers: Green with white letters
Orange with black lettering
Yellow with black letters
White with red letters
questions.explanation: Construction signs have black lettering on an orange background. While most warning signs are yellow, construction and maintenance warning signs are orange.

questions.question: Which statement about pavement markings is correct?
answers: White and yellow lines both prohibit passing
Solid yellow lines may be crossed to pass
White lines separate opposite directions; yellow lines separate same direction
White lines separate same direction; yellow lines separate opposite directions
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic going the same direction. Yellow lines separate traffic flowing in opposite directions. Broken lines indicate passing or lane changing is permitted if the way is clear, while a solid yellow line means no passing or lane changing.

questions.question: A broken line indicates that:
answers: No passing is permitted in either direction
Passing or lane changing is hazardous
The speed limit is 15 mph
Passing or lane changing is allowed when clear
questions.explanation: A broken (dashed) line permits passing or lane changing when the way is clear. A solid white line, by contrast, means passing or lane changing is hazardous, and a solid yellow line means no passing or lane changing at all except when turning left into or from an alley, private road or driveway.

questions.question: A solid yellow line indicates no passing or lane changing. Which of the following is an exception to that rule?
answers: Changing lanes to pass a stopped school bus
Turning left into or out of an alley or driveway
Passing a slow-moving vehicle
Passing a vehicle that is turning left
questions.explanation: Solid yellow lines indicate no passing or lane changing — unless making a left turn into or from an alley, private road or driveway.

questions.question: When the word ONLY is used on an overhead lane sign, you:
answers: Must go only in the direction the arrow points
May go in any direction available in that lane
Must stop before proceeding
May turn right if it is safe to do so
questions.explanation: Overhead lane signs tell you what direction you must go. When the word ONLY is used, you must go in the direction the arrow points; there is no other option.

questions.question: At a red light, you may turn right:
answers: Never, under any circumstances
Any time, without stopping or yielding
After stopping and yielding, unless a sign prohibits it
Only if you are the first vehicle in line and signal
questions.explanation: You can turn right at a RED light unless there is a sign that prohibits the turn. You may turn RIGHT only after STOPPING AND YIELDING to persons and other vehicles.

questions.question: A flashing red traffic light has the same meaning as:
answers: A YIELD sign
A stop sign
A caution light
A warning sign
questions.explanation: Flashing red light: You must come to a complete stop before entering the intersection. This light has the same meaning as a STOP sign.

questions.question: Which statement about traffic signals is correct?
answers: A green arrow lets you turn without stopping, but you must yield
A red arrow permits turning when the light is red
An amber light means you may enter without slowing
A green light means you never yield to anyone
questions.explanation: A GREEN arrow means that you may turn in the direction shown by the arrow without stopping if the way is clear. You MUST yield the right of way to persons and other traffic within the intersection. An amber light means you must stop before entering the intersection if at all possible.

questions.question: Crossbuck signs at a railroad crossing are:
answers: Detour signs
Stop signs
Advisory signs only
Yield signs
questions.explanation: Crossbuck signs are yield signs. You are legally required to yield the right of way to trains.

questions.question: Advance warning signs at a railroad crossing advise you to:
answers: Stop and wait for the gates to rise
Slow down, look, listen, and prepare to stop
Cross only if no train is visible
Stop and shift into low gear
questions.explanation: Advance warning signs come before the crossing itself, so they advise rather than command: slow down, look and listen for the train, and be prepared to stop. Once at the crossing you must obey the crossbuck, the flashing red lights and any gates.

questions.question: When the flashing red light signals at a railroad crossing are flashing, you must:
answers: Stop, and check all tracks before crossing
Proceed if no train is visible
Proceed only after the gate begins to rise
Stop and sound your horn
questions.explanation: When the lights are flashing, STOP! A train is approaching. You are legally required to yield the right of way to the train. If there is more than one track, make sure all tracks are clear before crossing.

questions.question: When gates are down at a highway-rail intersection, you should:
answers: Stop on the tracks and call 911
Drive around the gates
Proceed if no train is in sight
Wait for the gates and lights to stop
questions.explanation: When gates are down, realize the road is closed. Stop and wait until the gates go up and the red lights stop flashing before proceeding. NEVER drive around gates.

questions.question: The two-second following distance rule means you should:
answers: Stay two seconds behind only in heavy traffic
Stay two car lengths behind the vehicle ahead
Stay two seconds behind in rain, four on snow, six on ice
Stay at least two seconds behind, counting from a fixed point
questions.explanation: Scan ahead for a fixed point such as a pole, shadow, or pavement marking. When the rear bumper of the vehicle ahead passes the fixed point, start counting the number of seconds it takes you to reach the same point.

questions.question: According to the manual, you must allow at least two seconds of following distance for each ____ of vehicle length.
answers: 100 feet
20 feet
10 feet
40 feet
questions.explanation: YOU MUST ALLOW AT LEAST TWO SECONDS FOLLOWING DISTANCE FOR EACH 20 FEET OF VEHICLE LENGTH.

questions.question: Bus drivers should stay at least how many seconds back, and tractor-trailer drivers at least how many seconds back?
answers: Six seconds and eight seconds
Three seconds and four seconds
Four seconds and six seconds
Two seconds and three seconds
questions.explanation: If you are driving a car, stay at least two seconds back from the vehicle ahead. Bus drivers should stay at least four seconds back and tractor-trailer drivers at least six seconds back.

questions.question: You should triple the number of seconds of following distance when:
answers: You are carrying a heavier than normal load
It is at night
The roads are wet
The roads are covered with snow and slush
questions.explanation: Double the number of seconds when the roads are wet, when you are carrying a heavier than normal load, or at night (cars, four seconds). Triple the number of seconds when the roads are covered with snow and slush (cars, six seconds). Quadruple when ice covers the road (cars, eight seconds).

questions.question: Defensive drivers scan at least how far ahead?
answers: 10 to 15 seconds
20 to 30 seconds
One minute
5 to 10 seconds
questions.explanation: Defensive drivers scan at least 10 to 15 seconds ahead. If you're watching far enough ahead, you will count past one thousand and ten before passing a fixed object.

questions.question: If you cannot see clearly at night, the manual says it makes sense to increase your following distance to at least:
answers: One second
Three or four seconds
Six seconds
Two seconds
questions.explanation: At night your headlights show you only a limited distance ahead. The manual warns that driving faster than 55 mph at night means you cannot stop within the distance you can see, so when visibility is poor, increase your following distance to at least three or four seconds.

questions.question: A No-Zone is:
answers: A paved area where parking is prohibited
A heavy vehicle's blind spot along its sides or behind it
The blind spot of a motorcycle
The area near your rear corners hidden from your mirrors
questions.explanation: No-Zone covers both the large blind spots along either side of a heavy vehicle and the area directly behind it. Avoid tailgating and do not loiter alongside a truck: if the truck driver cannot see you, the driver cannot take evasive action if something appears in the road ahead.

questions.question: Some double trailer rigs can be as much as how long?
answers: 75 feet
150 feet
100 feet
50 feet
questions.explanation: Take into account the vehicle's total length, particularly rigs with double trailers. Some can be as much as 100 feet long.

questions.question: When you see the slow-moving vehicle symbol on the back of a vehicle ahead, it means the vehicle:
answers: Cannot travel faster than 25 mph
Cannot travel faster than 35 mph
Is a school bus
Is stopped in the roadway
questions.explanation: When you see this symbol on the back of a vehicle ahead, it is a warning to slow down. It means the vehicle cannot travel faster than 25 miles per hour.

questions.question: If your vehicle is disabled and you must walk where there are no sidewalks, you should walk:
answers: In the center of the roadway
Along the median
On the right side of the road, facing away from traffic
On the left side of the road, facing traffic
questions.explanation: If your vehicle is disabled and you must walk where there are no sidewalks, walk on the left side of the road facing traffic. At night, wear light-colored clothing.

questions.question: Under Wyoming's Move Over Law, on a highway with two or more lanes traveling in the same direction, when a stopped emergency vehicle or authorized maintenance vehicle has its lights or emergency signals activated, you should, as soon as it is safe:
answers: Sound your horn and pass immediately
Pull onto the shoulder and stop
Do nothing if you are on a two-lane road
Merge into the farthest lane or one lane apart
questions.explanation: When driving on an interstate highway or other highway with two or more lanes traveling in the same direction, the driver shall merge into the lane farthest from the vehicle or at least one lane of traffic apart from the vehicle.

questions.question: If a collision with an animal on or near the roadway seems inevitable, you should:
answers: Swerve suddenly to avoid the animal
Flash your headlights to make it move
Brake hard but keep the vehicle under control
Sound your horn and steer off the road
questions.explanation: If a collision seems inevitable, don't swerve suddenly to avoid the animal. Your risk of personal injury may be greater if you do. Brake as quickly as you safely can, but keep your vehicle under control and on the road.

questions.question: Headlights must be used from one-half hour after sunset until:
answers: Sunrise
One-half hour before sunrise
One hour before sunrise
Midnight
questions.explanation: Headlights must be used from one-half hour after sunset until one-half hour before sunrise, and at any other time when poor light or weather makes persons and vehicles hard to see 1,000 feet ahead.

questions.question: You should dim your high beams at least how far before meeting an oncoming vehicle?
answers: 300 feet
100 feet
200 feet
500 feet
questions.explanation: Use low beams when following other vehicles, when meeting oncoming vehicles, and when driving in town. You should dim at least 500 feet (about four to five seconds) before meeting an oncoming vehicle.

questions.question: If you are within 300 feet of the rear of a vehicle you are approaching, you should:
answers: Dim your lights to their lowest beam
Turn on your parking lights
Sound your horn
Use your high beams
questions.explanation: High beams in your mirror glare the driver ahead and make it harder for them to see. Dim to your lowest beam when following a vehicle, and any time you are within 300 feet of the vehicle you are approaching.

questions.question: You should never use parking lights while driving because:
answers: They burn out much faster than headlights
They drain the battery more than headlights
They are only permitted on farm vehicles and trailers
They are too dim to be seen in time and are illegal alone
questions.explanation: Parking lights are too dim to light the road or make you visible in time. Wyoming law also forbids driving with parking lights alone whenever headlights are required.

questions.question: When driving in fog, you should consider pulling off at the nearest safe spot and stopping when you cannot see:
answers: 30 seconds ahead
50 yards ahead
10 seconds ahead
5 seconds ahead
questions.explanation: When you cannot see at least 10 seconds ahead, consider pulling off at the nearest safe spot and stopping. In very heavy rain, snow or thick fog you may not be able to see more than 100 feet ahead, and at that point you cannot drive safely at any speed.

questions.question: The manual says to be careful during the first half hour after rain begins because:
answers: Windshield wipers work poorly when cold
Dust and oil mix with water and make the road slippery
Your tires are cold and have less grip
Drivers are more likely to speed in rain
questions.explanation: Be careful during the first half hour after the rain begins. Dust and oil mix with the water and make the roadway slippery.

questions.question: If you are stranded in a blizzard in your car, you should:
answers: Turn off the flashers to save the battery
Stay with the car and keep a window open
Run the engine and heater continuously
Leave the car and walk for help
questions.explanation: Do not panic. Stay with the car so you can be found more easily. Keep a window open for a bit of fresh air. Be aware of carbon monoxide — run the engine and heater sparingly, and only with a window open.

questions.question: When driving on snow or ice, the manual says you must:
answers: Use cruise control to maintain a steady speed
Change speed or direction suddenly to get around obstacles
Brake hard and firmly to stop quickly
Never lock your brakes, and do not use cruise control
questions.explanation: Never lock your brakes. You have no steering control unless the wheels are turning. DO NOT use cruise control.

questions.question: The law requires you to contact the police if there is an injury, a death, or property damage amounting to:
answers: $1,000 or more
$500 or more
$5,000 or more
$100 or more
questions.explanation: Contact the police if there is an injury, death or property damage amounting to $1,000 or more. The law requires you to give the police information on the crash at the time of the crash.

questions.question: If you damage an unattended vehicle or other property and cannot locate the owner, you must leave a note containing which of the following?
answers: The name and address of the owner of the property
Your name, address and telephone number
A money deposit to cover the damage
The names of any witnesses to the crash
questions.explanation: Leave on a piece of paper where the owner can find it: your name, address and telephone number; driver license number; license plate number; date and time of the crash; and damage to the vehicle. Then contact the nearest law enforcement agency.

questions.question: If you're involved in a crash, you must:
answers: Move injured people to the shoulder immediately
Stop and stay until police question everyone
Exchange information by mail within 30 days
Leave the scene and call your insurer from home
questions.explanation: If you are involved in a crash you must: stop your vehicle at or near the crash scene, and stay there until the police have arrived and questioned everyone involved.

questions.question: When a crash seems imminent, the manual says to do what, in order?
answers: Sound the horn, slow down, then turn away
Turn away, speed up, then slow down
Slow down, turn away, then speed up if appropriate
Speed up, slow down, then sound the horn
questions.explanation: Remember these three things in order: first, slow as fast as possible; second, turn away; third, when appropriate, speed up. Turning away and running off the road if necessary avoids a head-on crash, and speeding up is the alternative to avoid a side or rear impact.

questions.question: The manual's "If you begin to skid" guidance for a slippery road tells you to:
answers: Brake hard to stop the skid quickly
Turn into the skid and ease off the gas
Accelerate to pull out of the skid
Brake hard and steer opposite the skid
questions.explanation: The manual's slippery-road box says to keep your speed down, and if you begin to skid, to gently turn into the skid and ease your foot off the gas until you regain control. Note that the manual's separate "Skids" section advises keeping calm, not applying the brakes, and not oversteering.

questions.question: When using anti-lock brakes (ABS), you should:
answers: Apply hard, steady brake pressure
Pump the brakes once every second
Brake with one foot while steering with the other
Apply and release the brake pedal repeatedly
questions.explanation: Anti-lock brakes adjust automatically, so apply hard, steady brake pressure. Locked wheels and skids typically result when drivers jam on conventional brakes — pumping those brakes once every second is a good rule of thumb. But don't pump ABS brakes.

questions.question: If your brakes fail, you should:
answers: Turn off the ignition and wait for help to arrive
Pump the brakes, use the parking brake carefully, shift lower
Drive the car slowly to a garage for repairs
Sound the horn and hold the brake pedal down
questions.explanation: If your brakes fail: pump the brake pedal rapidly; use the parking brake, but hold the brake release so you can ease up on the brake if the rear wheels lock; shift to a lower gear; and do not try to drive the car to a garage.

questions.question: If you have a tire blowout, you should:
answers: Hold the wheel, go straight, and ease off the gas
Brake immediately and steer to the shoulder
Stop the car in the travel lane
Pull the parking brake and stop at once
questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel tightly, and keep the car going straight down the road. Ease your foot off the gas pedal but do not hit the brakes.

questions.question: If an oncoming or stopped vehicle suddenly appears in your lane of travel and there is immediate danger of a collision, you should:
answers: Flash your headlights and pass on the left
Sound your horn and continue straight
Steer off the road to the right
Brake as hard as possible and stay in your lane
questions.explanation: If an oncoming or stopped vehicle should suddenly appear in your lane of travel and there is immediate danger of a collision, STEER OFF THE ROAD TO THE RIGHT.

questions.question: If you are driving and see a disabled vehicle parked on the shoulder, you should:
answers: Stop on the shoulder behind it to help
Pass on the shoulder
Move to the left lane if possible
Sound your horn and slow down sharply
questions.explanation: If you are driving and see a disabled vehicle parked on the shoulder, move to the left lane if possible. The driver might not have seen you, and may open the door or pull onto the road.

questions.question: Under Wyoming law, a safety belt must be worn by:
answers: The driver only
Only the driver and front seat passengers on Interstate highways
All occupants of the vehicle, including the driver
Passengers over 12 years of age
questions.explanation: Under Wyoming law, a safety belt (seat belt) must be worn by all occupants of the vehicle, including the driver.

questions.question: Regarding the safety belt law, it is:
answers: The passenger's responsibility to wear a safety belt
Enforced only by the Department of Transportation
The driver's responsibility to see that the law is obeyed
The responsibility of the vehicle manufacturer
questions.explanation: It's the driver's responsibility to see that the law is obeyed. Children must be properly restrained in appropriate child-restraint systems.

questions.question: The lap belt should be:
answers: Worn only on the left side
Worn low across the soft part of the abdomen
Drawn snugly across the hip bones
Worn above the hip bones
questions.explanation: The lap belt should be drawn snugly across the hip bones. It should never be worn across the stomach or soft part of the abdomen. The shoulder strap should not be worn alone.

questions.question: According to the Wyoming Child Restraint Guide, the requirements apply to a child who has not reached his or her:
answers: Ninth birthday
Sixth birthday
Eighth birthday
Twelfth birthday
questions.explanation: Child who has not reached his/her ninth birthday. The requirements apply to all drivers, in privately owned, leased or rented non-commercial passenger vehicles, and to residents and non-residents.

questions.question: A child must be secured in a vehicle seat other than the front seat, except:
answers: When the child weighs more than 40 pounds
In a one-row vehicle or when all belts are in use
When the vehicle is a pickup truck
When the child is taller than five feet
questions.explanation: Child must be secured in vehicle seat other than front seat except in vehicles with one row of seats, or if all safety belts are in use by other child passengers.

questions.question: A child in a rear-facing infant seat shall not be placed:
answers: In the back seat of a sedan
In a vehicle with one row of seats
Beside a window
In front of an active airbag
questions.explanation: A rear-facing infant seat placed in front of an active airbag can be deadly, because the bag deploys into the back of the seat. This is why small children are secured in a vehicle seat other than the front seat.

questions.question: A child restraint must conform to which Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard?
answers: FMVSS 213
FMVSS 302
FMVSS 221
FMVSS 208
questions.explanation: The restraint itself has to meet the standard: it must conform to Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard 213 for child restraint systems. Using a seat that does not meet the standard does not satisfy the law.

questions.question: What are the maximum fines for non-use or misuse of a child restraint?
answers: $100 for a first offense, and $250 for second and subsequent offenses
$110 for a first offense, and $110 for second and subsequent offenses
$60 for a first offense, and $60 for second and subsequent offenses
$60 for a first offense, and $110 for second and subsequent offenses
questions.explanation: Maximum $60 fine for first offense. Fine shall be waived by the court upon receipt of proof of purchase, lease, or other acquisition, of an approved restraint after the offense occurred. Maximum $110 fine for second and subsequent offenses.

questions.question: Non-use or misuse of a child restraint is:
answers: Never a reason to stop a vehicle
Reasonable suspicion for a traffic stop
A primary offense only if a child is injured
Enforced only by local police
questions.explanation: Non-use or misuse is a primary offense: it is reasonable suspicion for stopping a vehicle to investigate a suspected violation.

questions.question: Which of the following is an exemption from the child restraint requirements?
answers: A child who weighs more than 40 pounds
A car with a single row of seats
A child who is eight years old
A physician's signed statement carried in the car
questions.explanation: Exemptions include a physician's signed statement, carried in the car, certifying that the child should not be secured in a child restraint system.

questions.question: A child within the age requirement is exempt from a child restraint system if:
answers: The child is sitting in the back seat
The child is taller than four feet nine inches
The lap and shoulder belt fit the child properly
The child weighs more than 40 pounds
questions.explanation: A child within the age requirement is exempt if the lap and shoulder belt fit properly across the collarbone, chest and hips and do not pose danger to the neck, face or abdomen in a crash or sudden stop.

questions.question: Which of the following persons is required to wear a safety belt?
answers: A passenger sitting in the back seat of a car in which the front seat occupants are wearing belts
A driver in a vehicle not required to be equipped with safety belts under federal law
A person with a written statement from a physician that it is not advisable to wear a safety belt for physical or medical reasons
A U.S. postal service worker performing duties as a postal carrier
questions.explanation: The others are all on the list of persons not required to wear a safety belt: those with a physician's written statement, those in a vehicle not required to be equipped with safety belts under federal law, and a U.S. postal service worker performing duties as a postal carrier.

questions.question: According to the booster seat hints, a belt-positioning booster for a child over 40 pounds should be used with:
answers: A lap belt only, worn low across the hips
A lap belt only, worn across the abdomen
A lap and shoulder belt, with the lap belt low across the hip
A shoulder belt only, worn snugly over the chest
questions.explanation: To fit a seat belt a child must: keep back and buttocks against the vehicle seat back; keep the shoulder belt on the shoulder resting snugly over the chest and the lap belt low across the hip/upper thigh; keep knees completely bent over the edge of the vehicle seat; and keep feet flat on the floor.

questions.question: A police officer has the right to stop you and inspect the equipment on your vehicle. If any equipment is defective, you will be:
answers: Directed to have it repaired immediately
Allowed to continue without repair
Required to sell the vehicle
Given a citation of 30 days
questions.explanation: If any equipment is defective, you will be directed to have it repaired immediately. If your vehicle is found to be unsafe you could be fined.

questions.question: In the penny test for tire tread wear, you:
answers: Hold the penny upside down by its tail
Press the edge of the penny into the sidewall
Scratch the tread with the edge of the penny
Put Lincoln's head into the lowest tread groove
questions.explanation: Take a penny and hold Abraham Lincoln's body between your thumb and forefinger. Select a point on your tire where the tread appears to be lowest and place Lincoln's head into one of the grooves.

questions.question: If you find yourself going the wrong way on an Interstate exit ramp, you should:
answers: Continue until you reach the next exit
Speed up to get off the ramp quickly
Pull onto the shoulder and turn around when clear
Turn around immediately as soon as you notice
questions.explanation: If you find yourself going the wrong way on a ramp, pull onto the shoulder and stop. Only turn around when there is no oncoming traffic, and never cross the median of an Interstate highway.

questions.question: If you miss your exit on the Interstate, you should:
answers: Cross the median to reach the exit
Stop and make a U-turn
Back up on the Interstate to return to the exit
Go on to the next exit
questions.explanation: If you MISS your exit, go on to the next exit. Backing up on the Interstate is dangerous. DO NOT cross the median of an Interstate highway.

questions.question: When approaching the Interstate on an entrance ramp, you should:
answers: Enter the Interstate at highway speed immediately
Check for a gap, adjust speed, signal, and merge at traffic speed
Merge without checking the shoulder for a gap in traffic
Sound your horn and merge as soon as possible
questions.explanation: As you approach the Interstate: CHECK over your shoulder for a gap in the traffic; ADJUST your speed to meet that gap and signal; DO NOT STOP unless there is no gap in traffic; and as you MERGE, make sure you are driving about the same speed as other traffic.

questions.question: You:
answers: May cross the median of an Interstate highway when you miss your exit
May cross the median at night only
Do not cross the median of an Interstate highway
May park on the median in an emergency
questions.explanation: DO NOT cross the median of an Interstate highway. Backing up on the Interstate is dangerous.

questions.question: When you wish to leave the Interstate, the manual instructs you to:
answers: Slow on the Interstate, then merge into the deceleration lane
Signal at the last possible moment and brake hard on the Interstate
Stop on the shoulder and wait for a gap
Never slow on the Interstate, and slow after turning into the deceleration lane
questions.explanation: PLAN ahead. Signal and move into the proper lane a mile or more before the exit. NEVER slow on the Interstate. SLOW after turning into the deceleration lane. Once off the Interstate, be aware of two-way traffic and check your speed.

questions.question: In the event of a breakdown or other emergency on the Interstate, you should:
answers: Pull onto the right shoulder with all four wheels off the road
Stand behind the vehicle and wave traffic around
Stop in the travel lane so others can call for help
Get out on the traffic side to flag down help
questions.explanation: Drive the vehicle as far onto the right shoulder as possible. Make certain that all four wheels are well off the road. Turn on your four-way emergency warning lights. Do not open the doors or get out on the traffic side of your vehicle.

questions.question: At what distance from a fire hydrant is parking prohibited?
answers: 10 feet
15 feet
20 feet
30 feet
questions.explanation: Do not park within 15 feet of a fire hydrant. Other prohibited parking places include driveways, bridges, tunnels, and disabled spaces without a placard or plate.

questions.question: If you park facing uphill where there is a curb, you should:
answers: Set the parking brake only, and leave the wheels as they are
Set the parking brake and turn the wheels away from the curb
Leave the engine running and turn the wheels to the right
Set the parking brake and turn the wheels towards the curb
questions.explanation: If you park facing uphill where there is a curb, you should set the parking brake and turn the wheels away from the curb. In any other situation, turn the wheels towards the curb or edge of the road.

questions.question: To leave a parking space, you should:
answers: Signal only if you are turning the wheel
Enter traffic without yielding to oncoming vehicles
Signal, yield to oncoming traffic, and do not dart out
Pull out as quickly as possible to beat traffic
questions.explanation: CHECK to see if anyone is coming. SIGNAL before you start to move. YIELD the right of way to oncoming vehicles and motorcycles. ENTER traffic. Do not dart out into traffic.

questions.question: When driving past parked cars, which of the following is a clue that a car is about to pull out in front of you?
answers: The car is parked within 30 feet of you
The driver's side window is open
Exhaust from the tail pipe or brake lights
The engine is cold
questions.explanation: Check for clues such as: exhaust coming from the tail pipe; brake lights on, a turn signal flashing, or white back-up lights on; front wheels turning out; or a person sitting behind the wheel.

questions.question: When passing a heavy vehicle, you should be sure you can see what in your rearview mirror before pulling back into your lane?
answers: Both headlights and the entire cab
Nothing; pull back in immediately
The headlights only
The trailer only
questions.explanation: Because it takes longer to pass a large vehicle, you should maintain a consistent speed when passing and be sure you can see both headlights and the entire cab of the truck in your rearview mirror before pulling back into your lane.

questions.question: Wyoming law prohibits reading or sending a text message from a cell phone or other device while operating a vehicle. The manual recommends that operators:
answers: Text only while stopped at a red light
Pull off the highway and stop before calling or texting
Text at any time as long as they are not speeding
Text only if they are using hands-free service
questions.explanation: WYDOT recommends vehicle operators pull well off the highway and STOP before making a cellular call or texting. Always remember, your first responsibility when you are driving is to pay attention to the road.

questions.question: If you are stopped by the police while driving, the manual instructs you to:
answers: Turn on your flashers and wait in the vehicle
Get out immediately to show your license
Keep driving until the officer follows you
Stay in the car with your hands on the wheel
questions.explanation: Put your vehicle in park. Roll down your window, end phone calls, and turn down your radio. Do not exit your vehicle unless asked to do so. Keep your hands on the steering wheel so the officer can see them.

questions.question: You have the right to politely deny a request by a police officer to search your car. However, if probable cause is present, the officer:
answers: May only search the passenger compartment
Must obtain a warrant in every case before searching
Must leave your vehicle and call a supervisor
May search without your consent when probable cause exists
questions.explanation: You always have the right to politely deny a request to search your car. Probable cause is the exception: with probable cause that a crime has been committed, the officer has the right to search your vehicle without your consent.
